bounded_slice.candidate: RFC 9052 COSE_Sign1 specification-level binding of deterministic evidence bytes into an explicit signing input

primary_source.title: RFC 9052: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE): Structures and Process
inspected_scope: Section 4.3 externally supplied data only as needed for external_aad semantics

bounded_slice.tested_scope: Exactly one official primary source was inspected, following p1-sa-561. The test asked only whether deterministic evidence bytes from p1-sa-560 can be bound into an explicit COSE_Sign1 signing input without external execution handoff. No second public source, cryptographic execution, concrete CBOR encoder execution, digest computation, key generation, signing, verification, external service, protected-primary action, manual-user execution, scheduler mutation, or other-worker/downstream/O semantic input was consumed.
observations: RFC 9052 defines COSE_Sign1 as a CBOR array carrying Headers, payload as bstr or nil, and signature as bstr.
The protected header bucket is transported as the CBOR encoding of the protected map wrapped in a bstr; the exact protected byte string is used by the cryptographic serialization structure.

For COSE_Sign1, Sig_structure uses context text Signature1, body_protected as the protected-header bstr, external_aad as a bstr that defaults to zero length when not supplied, and payload as the full payload bstr; the signer-protected field used for COSE_Sign is omitted.
RFC 9052 defines ToBeSigned as the CBOR encoding of Sig_structure and then passes ToBeSigned to the selected signature algorithm.
bounded_slice.inference: Positive at the specification-binding level: the deterministic evidence-package bytes established as a serialization target in p1-sa-560 can be placed directly in the COSE_Sign1 Sig_structure payload field, with context Signature1, an exact protected-header byte string, and explicit external_aad (zero-length when unused). This yields an unambiguous specification for what must be signed without requiring an external execution handoff merely to define the signing input. Concrete ToBeSigned bytes still require a conforming CBOR encoder, and actual authenticity still requires cryptographic execution plus key/trust policy; those children remain unresolved.
bounded_slice.uncertainty: This invocation did not execute CBOR encoding or cryptography, so it does not prove that the scheduled Chat surface can reproduce exact ToBeSigned bytes or produce/verify a COSE_Sign1 signature. It also does not select an algorithm, key identity, replay/freshness policy, or external_aad application profile.

evidence_anchors.supports: protected bucket is CBOR-encoded map wrapped in bstr; empty protected bucket representation and Headers grammar
Sig_structure fields, Signature1 context, body_protected, omitted sign_protected for Sign1, external_aad, payload, ToBeSigned construction

bounded_slice.replayability: A conforming implementation can reconstruct the same logical Sig_structure inputs from the fixed deterministic evidence bytes, exact protected-header bytes, explicit external_aad, and Signature1 context. Byte-for-byte ToBeSigned replay remains contingent on concrete deterministic CBOR encoding execution, which was not tested here.
